help.body:
{app} {version}

Manage Brave's native profiles from a single window: see which ones are open, switch with a click or a shortcut, and customise name, colour, icon, image and order.

Cards

  • The icons of an open card activate, minimise or restore, maximise and close its window; … lists every window when the profile has several.
  • Drag a card to another position to reorder the gallery.
  • Right click a card (or use the customisation panel) to change its name, colour, icon or image.
  • The last card groups the unassigned windows: assign one to a profile or save it as a new profile.
  • The language selector is in the header; every language is a JSON file in the locales folder.
  • The tray icon is always there: click it to jump to another profile, double click to open this window maximised. Closing the window keeps the app in the tray.

How each window is identified

Chromium runs every window of every profile of the same data folder inside one single process, and it does not publish any X11 property that says which profile a window came from. That is why the app learns the relation: it remembers the windows it opened, it deduces the profile when only one is active, and it lets you assign the rest by hand.

Shortcuts

  • Ctrl+Alt+1…9: activate the profile in that position.
  • Ctrl+Alt+Tab / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Tab: next or previous profile.

Privacy

The app does not read cookies, passwords or history, does not modify Local State nor the internal profile databases, does not intercept traffic and does not share folders between profiles. It only reads the visible name of the profiles, lists the processes and the windows, and reads the title of the open tabs when Brave runs in accessibility mode.
tray.still_running: Brave Workspace Manager keeps running in the tray. Click the icon to switch profiles, double click to open it, or choose Quit in its menu.
